interface.title: PlasmidNET – Dashboard
interface.field: Microbiology / plasmid genomics and antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) epidemiology
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory data analysis of a pre-built plasmid database, plus checks on single sequences (circular map, comparison, natural-vs-engineered scoring)
interface.what_it_is_for: A tabbed Dash/Plotly dashboard for browsing a local PLSDB/NCBI plasmid database: composition, host taxonomy, AMR genes, Inc/MOB typing, cross-feature correlations, geography over time and single-plasmid circular maps, with sequence comparison, sequence engineering analysis, an API explorer and CSV export.

data.note: The seeded SQLite database holds 38 plasmids (30 from PLSDB, 8 from NCBI), with accessions CP100001.1–CP100030.1. The Compare and Seq Analysis tabs were run on the uploaded test file example_plasmids.fasta (pPN1_natural_like at 552 bp, pPN2_cloning_vector_like at 387 bp). Some panels show hard-coded or precomputed figures that do not match the 38-plasmid database, for example the '57,751 geolocated plasmids' line (screens/026.webp), the '15,000 plasmids' UMAP (screens/037.webp) and the '182,362 complete plasmids' in the About text (screens/061.webp).

features.name: Circular feature map with hover details and a typing card panel
features.general: Enter an identifier, draw a ring map of one record's annotated regions coloured by category, hover a region for its name, function, class and coordinates, and read summary attribute cards below
features.specific: Plasmid Architecture Viewer: type an accession, press Visualize, see the AMR/MOB count chips and the polar ring of AMR (red) and MOB (orange) arcs (the only tracks drawn for seeded records; CDS, GC-ring, TA, virulence and QAC tracks were not seen), hover an arc (e.g. blaKPC-2, carbapenem, 1,000–1,900 bp), read the Inc/relaxase/MPF/oriT/mobility/host-range/pMLST cards, and use the link to PLSDB
steps: type an accession such as CP100001.1
press Visualize
read the feature-count chips and centre label (length, topology, GC, species)
hover an arc for gene details
scroll to the MOB Typing & Incompatibility cards
serves_tasks: Draw a circular feature map of one record and read its typing summary
Repeat the map for another record, including a short linear one

features.name: Animated cumulative bubble map with year slider and subgroup selector
features.general: Show cumulative counts per region as sized and coloured bubbles on a world map, scrub through years with a slider or play the animation, and redraw the animation for one chosen subgroup
features.specific: Temporal Spread Animations: drag the year slider (2003–2024) or press ▶/◼ on the All Plasmids map, then pick an Inc group or mobility type in the dropdowns below to get a separate animated map for that subset
steps: drag the year slider to a year
press ▶ Play to animate, ◼ to stop
choose an Inc group in Inc Group Spread
choose a mobility type in Mobility Type Spread
read the subgroup's own animated map
serves_tasks: Restrict the spread animation to one subgroup

features.name: Point map coloured by category, with legend filtering and hover
features.general: Plot each sequence at its sampling location coloured by a category, hover a point for its identifier and attributes, and click legend entries to hide or show categories
features.specific: Global Plasmid Map by Mobility: hover a dot for accession, mobility, country and rep_type; click 'non-mobilizable' in the legend to grey it out; zoom and reset with the mode bar
steps: hover a dot
click a legend entry to toggle that category
wheel or mode-bar to zoom
press reset view
serves_tasks: Map individual sequences by sampling location coloured by a category, and filter categories

features.name: Natural-vs-engineered sequence scorer
features.general: Load a sequence (fetch by ID, upload a file, or paste into an editable box), run a scan, and get a 0–100 engineered-likelihood score with evidence: restriction-site table, motif counts, k-mer naturalness metrics, detected cloning scars and score reasoning
features.specific: Seq Analysis: Fetch & Analyze by NCBI accession, or upload FASTA/GenBank into the textarea, or edit it, then press Analyze Sequence to see the score badge, chips (restriction sites/kb, RE hotspots, promoters, RBS, vector signatures, IS/Tn, eng. scars), the Restriction Sites table, K-mer Naturalness Analysis, Engineering Junction Scars and Score Reasoning. Multi-record FASTA is scored as one merged sequence, so keep one record in the box
steps: upload a FASTA (or paste or fetch)
edit the textarea to keep one record
press Analyze Sequence
read the score and the 'Natural' / 'Likely engineered' label
review the restriction-site table, k-mer metrics and scars
serves_tasks: Score whether a sequence looks natural or engineered, with supporting evidence
Repeat per record to compare a natural and an engineered sequence

features.name: Multi-sequence comparison ring plot with per-sequence export
features.general: Supply several sequences by ID list or file upload, run a pairwise alignment, draw them as concentric or adjacent tracks on one circular plot, and download each as FASTA or annotated GenBank
features.specific: Plasmid Comparison: enter accessions (one per line) or upload FASTA/GenBank, press Compare, see the length chips and the pyCirclize ring plot plus the BLASTn status line (here 'No BLASTn alignments found'), then use the FASTA/GenBank buttons in Download Annotations
steps: upload FASTA or list accessions
press Compare
read the per-sequence chips and ring plot
read the alignment status
download FASTA or GenBank per sequence
serves_tasks: Lay several sequences on a shared circular plot, attempt a pairwise alignment, and export them

features.name: Endpoint query explorer with JSON and table output
features.general: Pick a query type from a list, enter a term, run it, and see the raw JSON response alongside a rendered results table
features.specific: API Explorer: Endpoint dropdown (Search plasmids, AMR by gene, AMR by drug class, Typing by Inc group, Taxonomy by genus, Plasmid details…), Query box, Run, then the JSON block and table
steps: choose an endpoint
type a query term
press Run
read the JSON count/results and the table
serves_tasks: Run a structured query against the database and see raw plus tabular results

features.name: Category lookup by group name
features.general: Type a higher-level or lower-level organism group name and get a count of matching records, with a link to the external source
features.specific: Explore by Taxonomy: Genus and/or Species text boxes, Search, then 'Found N plasmids for X' and a View in PLSDB button. The Species box matches the epithet only: 'coli' finds 4, 'Escherichia coli' finds nothing
steps: type a genus, or a species epithet alone
press Search
read the count message
follow View in PLSDB
serves_tasks: Find which host organisms carry the most sequences, and look up an organism group by name
Repeat the lookup at the species level

features.name: Dataset picker with CSV download
features.general: Choose one of several prepared tables from a dropdown and download it as CSV
features.specific: Export Data footer: select All Plasmids, MOB Typing & Inc Groups, AMR Annotations, Geographic Data or NCBI Extra Plasmids, then press Download CSV
steps: open the Export Data dropdown
choose a dataset
press Download CSV
serves_tasks: Download a dataset as a table

features.name: Embedding scatter with box zoom and hover
features.general: Show records in a 2-D embedding coloured by a category, drag a box to zoom into a cluster, and hover points for identifiers and attributes
features.specific: Plasmid Feature Space (UMAP), coloured by mobility and by host genus: a precomputed 15,000-plasmid embedding, not the 38-plasmid local database (hovered points such as NZ_CP107400.1 are not seeded records). hover a point

read cell counts in the drug class x Inc group heatmap
compare the grouped bars for each mobility class
read the same layout in Geography for country and host
